title: Jump, DRW Bet on New Compute Market as AI Boom Faces Scrutiny
key_facts: TokenPost, 17 Oct: Jump Trading plans to use its balance sheet to take positions in over-the-counter contracts, perpetual futures and prediction bets tied to computing capacity.
Itô Markets co-founders Affaan Mustafa and Alejandro Soumah Fernandez joined Jump to lead the business.
DRW signed a GPU-as-a-Service agreement with QumulusAI for a dedicated cluster of Nvidia Blackwell B300 chips: a one-year term with three one-year renewal options.
DRW and Jump co-led Silicon Data's $4.7 million seed round in 2025; Silicon Data builds GPU rental price indexes.
CME Group's proposed futures would reference Silicon Data's daily rental indexes for Nvidia H100 and B200 GPUs; each contract covers 730 GPU-hours and monthly contracts run 36 months out.
CME first targeted a 5 Oct launch subject to regulatory review; the launch is now planned for later this year.

why_it_matters_hint: Trading firms are building a market where AI computing power can be priced, bought and sold like a commodity.
